nina: Quick bring-up notes for Saturn-14B (fp16 / int8 / int6 hybrid). Ran focused slices: long-form summarization (N=150), multi-turn retrieval-QA (N=120), short assistant chat (N=230).

kevin: nice. highlight the main tradeoffs + a tiny scorecard pls.

nina: short table (avg across slices): ROUGE-L / BLEURT / p50 latency @1024 / est cost($/1k tokens)

nina: ```
variant | ROUGE-L | BLEURT | p50 latency(ms) | cost($/1k)
fp16    | 0.765   | 0.88   | 145             | 1.00
int8    | 0.758   | 0.86   | 115             | 0.68
int6    | 0.752   | 0.85   | 100             | 0.57
hybrid  | 0.754   | 0.85   | 105             | 0.60

deltas (int6 vs fp16): -1.7% ROUGE-L, -3.4% BLEURT, -31% latency, -43% cost
```

rohit: what's the hybrid variant? how'd you route?

nina: hybrid = default int6, but for requests with both (1) input_tokens > 600 OR (2) tag: "high_precision", we call fp16. For short chats we keep int6. This aims to capture long-doc QA quality while optimizing bulk traffic.

anya: failure modes at int6? any specific categories?

nina: quick breakdown from triage (int6 regressions on long-doc QA):
- 55%: missing intermediate reasoning steps (abstractive compression)
- 30%: subtle factual shifts (dates/percentages)
- 15%: brevity/tone differences (more terse)

kevin: latency tail numbers? 95/99p?

nina: 95p: fp16 390ms, int8 320ms, int6 290ms, hybrid 300ms. 99p: fp16 720ms, int6 540ms, hybrid 560ms. Hybrid tracks int6 closely except when fp16 is selected.

rohit: economics: what does this buy us if we flip 70% traffic to hybrid?

nina: quick econ sketch: baseline all fp16 = $140k/month. If traffic mix --> hybrid 70% / int8 20% / fp16 10% => ~$95k/month (~32% savings). After a 12% quality rollback buffer -> plan $106k/month.

kevin: product asks: can we set rollout gates? what's a simple scorecard for GTN to accept hybrid?

rohit: propose gating rules:
- Allow hybrid if ROUGE-L drop <= 2% absolute on holdout long-doc slice AND BLEURT delta <= 3% AND hallucination (measured by unit-checks) increase <= 2 percentage points.
- Also require prometheus alert for hallucination rate > 2.5% on canary.

anya: ops notes: need to ensure int6 kernels available in our dedicated fleets; also verify memory packing improvements don't cause evictions for heavy batchers. Recommend small canary (3% traffic) + 24h shadowing.

nina: sample routing rule (JSON):
```json
{"routing": {"default_model": "saturn-14b-int6", "rules": [{"match": {"input_tokens_gt": 600}, "model": "saturn-14b-fp16"}, {"match": {"request_tag": "high_precision"}, "model": "saturn-14b-fp16"}]}}
```

kevin: can we get a more granular eval for multi-turn retrieval-QA specifically? product wants precision@k and hallucination counts.

nina: yes I’ll run a 1k-sample focused eval for retrieval-QA (precision@1/3, hallucination checks). will post results in 48h.

ci-bot: Canary created: canary/saturn-hybrid-2024-06-11 (traffic 3%). Dashboard: /deploys/4310

kevin: perfect. please add auto-eval hooks that fail rollout if hallucination > 2pp or ROUGE-L drop > 2% after 24h.

nina: added CI hooks and a follow-up ticket: ENG-ML-5421. tagging GTN for review.

anya: thanks — will coordinate infra readiness for int6 kernels and dedicated pool scheduling.

rohit: nice work. once the 24h canary passes we can prepare a short slide for the GTN pricing deck showing savings + risk controls. :rocket:
